seriesLong: Milano-Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics: final medal table
asOf: Final table, 22 February 2026. Ordered by gold medals first, then silver, then bronze — the standard Olympic ranking, which is why the Netherlands finish above Italy on ten golds each.

next.summary: Milano-Cortina is finished — it was held from 6 to 22 February 2026. The next Games are the summer ones in Los Angeles, and the next winter ones are in the French Alps four years from now.
rows: 4 Oct – 21 Nov 2027 — South Africa, Zimbabwe, Namibia
next.caution: The French Alps Games are the first to be awarded to a region rather than a host city. Note the pile-up in the autumn of 2027: the athletics, rugby and cricket world championships all land within weeks of each other, and two of them overlap almost completely.
next.checked: Dates checked twice each against separate searches on 11 September 2026.

footnote: Norway's eighteen golds are the most any country has won at a single Winter Games, and its forty-one medals are a record too. The United States finished second on its own best winter return, twelve golds and thirty-three medals. Every row here adds up: golds plus silvers plus bronzes equals the total, in all ten cases, which is the first check we run on a table like this.
